texts: good. parses as a fireable rule with the heir, the station and the retiring Keeper all minted fresh per retirement.
good. same clean shape as the retirement sentence - the death is the trigger, and the heir and the inherited station are bound per occurrence.

bad: "A Keeper's family ..." with an ordinary verb reads as one particular Keeper rather than as a standing law, so the general rule you intend is not licensed by the wording (the parse had to invent a universal the sentence never states). Rewrite as: "Every Keeper's family keeps that Keeper's inherited station." - the explicit "every" licenses the general rule and lets "that Keeper" bind back to it.
good. parses as a fireable rule obliging the Council to approve each station transfer, with "any" recorded as the quantifier word.
